title: Action of 27 June 1798
text: The action of 27 June 1798 was a single-ship action fought between the British and French navies in the Strait of Sicily as part of the Mediterranean campaign of 1798. On 19 May 1798, a French fleet left Toulon to invade Egypt. On 12 June the French fleet captured Malta, after which the 32-gun frigate Sensible, captained by Frigate Captain Guillaume-François-Joseph Bourdé, was detached from the fleet to transport wounded troops and loot back to France. Meanwhile, the 38-gun British frigate HMS Seahorse, under Captain Edward Foote, was detached from the Mediterranean Fleet in the Tagus River with orders to reinforce Sir Horatio Nelson's fleet, which was searching for the French fleet.
